author: Brian Hawken
text: It can take 12-48hrs for the two readings to "align" as your body is still getting used to a foreign object inside it.  CGM will usually have a variant from the fingerstick even after this time, and usually lags from about 15 minutes from the fingerstick reading (imagine a train and the fingerstick is the lead car and the CGM is the caboose - the fingerstick may read high but the caboose has not gotten there yet, same with a low, etc.).  That said, you can get them pretty consistent out of the gate if you "soak" the sensor.  On your next sensor, apply the new one 24hrs before the old one expires (but do not activate it).  Once the original expires activate your new one.  This will have given your body time to adjust to it and the numbers will start out much more consistent.  The missing spike can be  because the spike was false and the algorithm corrected the readings on the graph.  It takes a minute to live with it and get used to the rythms each CGM has.  If ever in doubt - the fingerstick is the accurate reading as it truly measures your blood while CGM is using an algorithm measuring subcuntaneous fluid.  Best of luck and 🙌 to the little one for being so brave!
